question.text: Hitler's Nazi Germany carried out this genocide during which over ten million civilians were killed. Among those targeted were Jews, Gypsies, and homosexuals.
question.clue: Adolf Eichmann was one top official involved in this event, as was a man known as the "Angel of Death," Josef Mengele.

swap.leadin: Tsar Nicholas II and this man sent each other a series of ten telegrams in summer 1914 as their countries teetered on the brink of war.
swap.text: Nicholas II corresponded with this man, his cousin and the last Kaiser of Germany.
swap.clue: In an 1897 speech, this leader's foreign minister Bernhard von Bulow outlined how this ruler's nation wanted its "place in the sun."

question.leadin: This leader argued that "the great questions of the day will not be decided through speeches and decisions, but by iron and blood."
question.text: Name this Prussian statesman, known as the Iron Chancellor, whose philosophy of Realpolitik succeeded in unifying Germany in the 19th century.
question.clue: This man edited the Ems Dispatch to provoke the Franco-Prussian War.

swap.leadin: Give the following about early Protestantism.
swap.text: Luther's break from the Catholic Church began this period of religious history, in which Protestants tried to change the workings of the church.
swap.clue: A leader of this movement feuded with Huldrych Zwingli (ULD-rik ZVING-lee) in the Marburg Colloquy.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the anti-communist revolutions of 1989.
question.text: While communist regimes toppled around the world, this German Cold War landmark stood until November 1989, when a confusing statement by Gunter Schabowski caused protesters to tear it down piece by piece.
question.clue: The construction of this object created "ghost stations" in which subways on certain lines would not stop.

swap.text: This city is located in Germany's southeast. It is the capital of the state of Bavaria and is the home of BMW.
swap.clue: That used in Rollerball is the BMW Headquarters and Museum.

question.leadin: This event was ostensibly a reaction to the murder of Ernst vom Rath.
question.text: Name this November 1938 pogrom, in which the Nazi SA destroyed synagogues and Jewish businesses around Germany. Either the German or the English name is acceptable.
question.clue: This event occurred after a failed assassination attempt on Count Johannes von Welczeck ("vell-check"), in which Ernst vom Rath was killed by Herschel Grynszpan.

swap.leadin: Name these leaders of various instances of Germany.
swap.text: This pal of Erich Ludendorff was the last president of the Weimar republic, and basically handed Hitler power in his old age. He was a heroic commander during World War I.
swap.clue: This man was reviled by Hitler, who referred to him as "that old fool" and "that old reactionary" during his time as president of the Weimar ] Republic.

question.leadin: This battle began when Russian commander Peter Wittgenstein attacked Napoleon's right wing near Leipzig.
question.text: Name this 1813 battle which halted the advance of the Sixth Coalition.
question.clue: The defender's left side was commanded by Heinrich Holk until reinforcements arrived from nearby Halle led by Pappenheim, who was later killed.

swap.leadin: Name these questionable items of correspondence from European history.
swap.text: This falsified transcript of a meeting between Kaiser Wilhelm I and French ambassador Benedetti enraged France into war with Prussia.
swap.clue: This document led to the eventual downfall of the man responsible for the creation of the "Liberal Empire," Emile Ollivier, while the Havas printing of this document notably failed to translate the word "adjutant."

question.text: The war was ended by this treaty, which also recognized Prussia's conquest of Silesia.
question.clue: Madras was transferred to the British after a short French rule as a provision of this Treaty, whose other terms included the transfer of some Italian duchies to Spain. It essentially reverted to the terms established by the Treaty of Utrecht

swap.text: Among the various construction projects that Ludwig undertook was this castle, which is located close to the Hohenschwangau Castle where Ludwig grew up. Ludwig was inspired by the Singers' Hall of Wartburg Castle when cooking up his plans for this castle.

question.text: Germany prescribed Pervitin en masse to its troops during an invasion of this region. This Czech region was annexed by Germany prior to World War II.
question.clue: This majority German-speaking territory that was handed over in the Munich Pact, a cession that Neville Chamberlain claimed had brought "peace for our time."

swap.leadin: One member of this family secretly purchased the captured crown jewels of Charles the Bold from the city of Basel.
swap.text: Name this German banking family based in Augsburg which reached its height under Jakob and dominated European business during the 15th and 16th centuries.
swap.clue: Archduke Sigismund granted a member of this family control over Tyrol's silver mines after that member of this family loaned Sigismund a huge number of florins.

question.text: Due to this action, Scapa Flow is the source for much of the world's steel with low levels of background radiation. This action made Scapa Flow a popular diving location and was taken a week before the signing of the Treaty of Versailles.
question.answerHtml: scuttling of the High Seas Fleet [accept answers indicating the scuttling of the Imperial German Navy]
question.answer: scuttling of the High Seas Fleet

swap.text: As early as 1834, this Friedrich List-advocated customs union of German-speaking states, excluding Austria, provided a common market over much of Europe.
swap.clue: Karl Bruck advocated the entry of Austria, but this plan was halted by the minister of commerce, Delbruck.

question.leadin: Targets of this event included its namesake, who was nicknamed "The Harpist," and General Kuno Graf von Moltke, who was called "Sweetie."
question.text: Name this 1907 affair centering on accusations by a journalist about the homosexuality of members of Kaiser Wilhelm II's inner circle.
question.clue: Kuno von Moltke was one of several advisors to Wilhelm II who were accused of being practicing homosexuals during this affair, which rocked pre-WWI Germany.

swap.leadin: Its first ruler was Otto of Scheyern, who in 1124 moved his family to their namesake castle on the Paar.
swap.text: Name this German noble house, which ruled Bavaria from 1180 until 1918.
swap.clue: Joseph II seized on the 1778 death of a member of this house to occupy their territory, only to be forced to withdraw by Frederick the Great in the Treaty of Teschen.

question.leadin: This polity came under the rule of the Franconian Hohenzollerns in 1415, after which it eventually came to dominate the Duchy of Prussia.
question.text: Name this polity corresponding to a modern German state surrounding Berlin. It lends its name to a famous neoclassical Gate in that city.
question.answerHtml: Margraviate of Brandenburg [Also accept March of Brandenburg or Electorate of Brandenburg.]
question.clue: A later (emphasize) elector of this state invited expelled French Huguenots to settle after the Edict of Fontainebleau and, thanks to his military successes in neighboring Pomerania, was called the "Great Elector".

swap.leadin: In The Man Without Qualities, a plan to buy Austrian oil fields is concocted by the character of Arnheim, whom critics felt represented this man.
swap.text: Name this Jewish opponent of Zionism, a Foreign Affairs minister who, two months after the signing of the Treaty of Rapallo, was assassinated by the ultra-nationalist Edwin Kern and Hermann Fischer.
